sections.title: Types of relationships
sections.content:
Advanced vocabulary helps describe the complexity of human connections:
• acquaintance — someone you know slightly. He's not a close friend, just an acquaintance.
• confidant — a trusted person you share secrets with. My sister has always been my closest confidant.
• mentor — an experienced advisor. She found a great mentor in her first year at work.
• rival — a competitor. The two companies have been rivals for decades.
• ally — a supportive partner or friend. Having strong allies at work makes difficult projects manageable.

sections.title: Describing bonds
sections.content:
The strength and nature of relationships can be expressed precisely:
• inseparable — always together. The twins were inseparable throughout childhood.
• estranged — no longer close, especially family. He's been estranged from his father for years.
• devoted — very loving and loyal. She was a devoted mother who sacrificed everything.
• mutual — shared by both sides. Their mutual respect made the partnership successful.
• platonic — close but not romantic. They maintained a purely platonic friendship.

sections.title: Social interactions
sections.content:
How we interact socially can be described in nuanced ways:
• bond with — form a close connection. She quickly bonded with her new colleagues.
• fall out with — have a disagreement that damages a relationship. He fell out with his business partner over money.
• confide in — trust someone with personal information. I only confide in people I truly trust.
• drift apart — gradually become less close. After university, many friends drift apart.

exercises.question: A person you know slightly but who isn't a close friend is an:
exercises.hint: Not quite a friend, but you recognise them.
exercises.explanation: An acquaintance is someone you know slightly but not well.

exercises.question: If two people gradually become less close over time, they:
exercises.explanation: Drift apart means to slowly become more distant from someone.

exercises.question: A friendship that is close but NOT romantic is described as:
exercises.explanation: Platonic describes a relationship that is intimate and affectionate but not sexual.

exercises.question: Someone who is no longer in contact with a family member is:
exercises.explanation: Estranged means no longer close to someone, especially a family member.

exercises.question: To share personal secrets with someone you trust is to:
exercises.explanation: Confide in means to tell someone about secret or private matters, trusting them.

exercises.question: A trusted person who gives you guidance based on experience is a:
exercises.explanation: A mentor is an experienced and trusted adviser.

exercises.question: If respect or admiration is shared by both people, it is:
exercises.hint: Both sides feel the same way.
exercises.explanation: Mutual means experienced or done by each of two or more parties toward the other.

exercises.question: To have a serious disagreement that harms a relationship is to:
exercises.hint: It's a sudden conflict, not gradual.
exercises.explanation: Fall out with means to have a quarrel or disagreement with someone.
